title: CCNP Enterprise vs CCNP Security
intro: The two biggest Cisco professional tracks, one decision: the routing/SD-x generalist road or the firewall/identity specialist road. Same exam economics, genuinely different careers.

a.name: CCNP Enterprise
a.tagline: ENCOR + concentration — routing, switching, SD-WAN, SD-Access. The broadest professional networking credential.

b.name: CCNP Security
b.tagline: SCOR + concentration — firewalls, ISE, VPN/SSE. The highest-paying CCNP track, tied to the Cisco security stack.

verdict: Follow the work, not the salary table. Enterprise is the broader bet: more postings, more employer types, and the natural home for route/switch careers heading toward architecture. Security pays more per posting (it's consistently the top-paying CCNP) but binds tighter to the Cisco security stack — its value tracks whether your employers run Secure Firewall and ISE. If your tickets are routing and WAN, Enterprise; if you're already elbow-deep in firewall policy and NAC, Security. And if 'security' to you means SOC work — alerts, forensics, hunting — neither: that's CCNP Cybersecurity, a different cert entirely.

rows.label: Structure & cost
rows.b: 350-701 SCOR ($400) + 1 concentration ($300) — 7 options until Aug 26, 2026, then 4

rows.label: 2026 disruption
rows.a: ENCOR v1.2 live since March: wireless removed, AI domain added
rows.b: Bigger: SCOR v2.0 launches Aug 27; three concentrations (SESA/SWSA/SVPN) retire Aug 26 with no replacements

rows.label: Job-posting footprint
rows.a: Broadest of any CCNP — named across enterprise, gov, MSP postings
rows.b: Fewer postings, higher pay per posting; concentrated in Cisco-security shops and federal/cleared work

rows.label: Salary band (third-party)
rows.b: ~$110–155K — consistently cited as the top-paying CCNP track

rows.label: Vendor lock sensitivity
rows.b: High — value tracks the employer's Cisco security footprint; weaker in Palo Alto/Fortinet estates

rows.label: Expert-tier runway
rows.a: ENCOR qualifies you for the CCIE Enterprise Infrastructure lab
rows.b: SCOR qualifies you for the CCIE Security lab

pick_a_if: Your daily work is routing, switching, WAN, or SD-x — the generalist infrastructure lane
You want maximum employer optionality and the architecture trajectory
Your market is mixed-vendor and you need skills that read everywhere
The automation direction appeals — ENAUTO double-counts and the v1.2 AI domain pushes you there anyway
pick_b_if: You already touch Cisco Secure Firewall, ISE, or VPN estates at work
Federal/cleared or Fortune-500 security engineering is the target — where this track's premium concentrates
You want the top-paying CCNP and your market genuinely runs the Cisco stack
CCIE Security is the plausible summit
both_note: Plenty of senior engineers hold both — typically Enterprise first (the fundamentals generalize) then Security when their role specializes. There's no shared exam between them, so budget both fully. And triple-check the timing if choosing Security in 2026: the Aug 26/27 version boundary decides your study materials.

faq.question: Isn't CCNP Security the same as cybersecurity?
faq.answer: This is the trap the names set: CCNP Security is network-security ENGINEERING — you build and run firewalls, identity systems, and VPN/SSE. SOC-style cybersecurity — triage, incident response, threat hunting — is CCNP Cybersecurity, the renamed CyberOps Professional and a completely separate certification. Three different certs, three different chairs; our guides cover all three.

faq.question: Which is harder?
faq.answer: Folklore calls them comparable with different textures: ENCOR is broad (six domains spanning routing to automation), SCOR is deep in an ecosystem (the whole Cisco security portfolio). The honest difficulty variable is your day job — engineers fail the track they don't practice. SCOR punishes people who've never touched a firewall exactly as ENCOR punishes people who've never run OSPF.

faq.question: Does one lead to better long-term careers?
faq.answer: Different ceilings, both high: Enterprise trends toward network architect (BLS's growing +12% column); Security trends toward security engineering leadership and, paired later with CISSP, the security-architecture world. The declining column — pure keep-the-lights-on administration — is the only trajectory to avoid, and both tracks escape it if you add automation.
